3001:
Inverse cosine needs its argument between -1 and 1, so -1 \leq \frac{4x+2[x]}{3} \leq 1 with [x] the greatest integer function
Write x = n+f where n = [x] is an integer and 0 \leq f < 1, giving -3 \leq 6n+4f \leq 3
Only n = -1 and n = 0 survive, yielding -\frac{1}{4} \leq x \leq \frac{3}{4}, so \alpha+\beta = \frac{1}{2}
Thus 12(\alpha+\beta) = 6, which matches option A → (A)
3002:
Equality |a+b| = |a|+|b| holds exactly when ab \geq 0, and here x^{2}+x-9 = x+(x^{2}-9)
So x(x^{2}-9) \geq 0 gives (x+3)x(x-3) \geq 0, hence x \in [-3,0] \cup [3,\infty)
Thus \alpha = -3 with \beta = 0 and \gamma = 3, so \alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha = 9
This value matches option B → (B)
3003:
|z+2| = |z-2| means z is equidistant from -2 and 2, so Re(z) = 0 and z = iy with y real
Then \frac{z+3}{z-i} = \frac{3+iy}{i(y-1)} = \frac{y}{y-1}-i\frac{3}{y-1}
An argument of \frac{\pi}{4} needs equal positive real and imaginary parts, so y = -3
Hence |z|^{2} = 9, which matches option A → (A)
3004:
Every map from a 4-element set to a 3-element set is free, giving 3^{4} = 81 functions
Onto maps use all three values, counted by \binom{4}{2} \times 3! = 36 after choosing the doubled value
Subtracting leaves 81-36 = 45 maps that miss at least one value
This count matches option B → (B)
3005:
By Cayley-Hamilton A^{2}-(a+d)A+(ad-bc)I = O, so matching A^{2}-4A+3I = O forces a+d = 4 and ad-bc = 3
With entries in {0,1,2,3,4} put d = 4-a, so bc = a(4-a)-3
Only a = 1 with bc = 0, a = 2 with bc = 1 and a = 3 with bc = 0 work, giving 9+1+9 pairs
The total 19 matches option D → (D)
3007:
With a = \frac{10}{3} write T = a+29d, so S = 15(a+T) = 50+15T and S = T^{3} gives T^{3}-15T-50 = 0
Factoring yields (T-5)(T^{2}+5T+10) = 0, whose only real root is T = 5
Then 29d = 5-\frac{10}{3} = \frac{5}{3}, giving d = \frac{5}{87} with all 30 terms non-negative
This value matches option A → (A)
3008:
All 7 people can queue in 7! = 5040 orders with no restriction
Treating the 3 girls as one block gives 5! orders of blocks times 3! internal orders, equal to 720 with all girls together
Subtracting gives 5040-720 = 4320 queues with the girls not all together
This count matches option D → (D)
3010:
Mean 40 over 9 entries gives a+b = 360-280 = 80 with known total 280
Median 21 across the ordered list forces b \leq 21 < a alongside a > b
Mean deviation 26 about the median gives |a-21|+|b-21| = 234-183 = 51, i.e. a-b = 51
Solving yields a = \frac{131}{2}, so 2a = 131

3011:
L_{1} is x = -3, meeting L_{2} at A = (-3,-3) and L_{3} at B = (-3,9)
The bisectors satisfy \frac{|x-y|}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{|3x+y|}{\sqrt{10}}, and the obtuse one meets x = -3 at C = (-3,3\sqrt{5}-6)
Then AC = 3(\sqrt{5}-1) and BC = 3(5-\sqrt{5}), so \frac{BC^{2}}{AC^{2}} = 5
This ratio matches option A → (A)
3012:
Midpoint (5,-1) of AB with A = (1,2) gives B = (9,-4), and centroid (3,4) gives C = (-1,14)
The perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC meet at the circumcenter (\frac{94}{7},\frac{215}{21})
Adding gives \alpha+\beta = \frac{497}{21}, so 21(\alpha+\beta) = 497
This value matches option C → (C)
3013:
A chord from (1,2) bisected by the y-axis at (0,k) has its other end at (-1,2k-2)
Lying on x^{2}+y^{2}+x-3y = 0 forces 4k^{2}-14k+10 = 0, so k = 1 or k = \frac{5}{2}
The ends are R = (-1,0) and S = (-1,3) with midpoint (-1,\frac{3}{2})
Hence 6(\alpha+\beta) = 3, which matches option B → (B)
3015:
Through (-2,-8,6) draw the line with direction (1,-1,2), namely (-2+t,-8-t,6+2t)
Meeting (1+s,1+2s,-s) needs 6+2t = -s with -2+t = 1+s, giving t = -1 and s = -4
The meeting point is (-3,-7,4), at squared distance 1+1+4 = 6 from (-2,-8,6)
This value matches option B → (B)
3016:
Since \frac{3-4\tan x}{4+3\tan x} = \tan(\alpha-x) with \tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}, the first term is the constant \alpha-x
With x = \sin\theta the bracket equals \tan\frac{\theta}{2}, so twice its arctan is \theta = \sin^{-1}x
Differentiating gives \frac{dy}{dx} = -1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}, equal to -1+2 = 1 at x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
This value matches option C → (C)
3018:
Both bounds are even, so the area doubles the x \geq 0 half, where the curves meet at x = \frac{\pi}{2}
On [0,\frac{\pi}{2}] the curve x\sin x sits below \pi-x, while on [\frac{\pi}{2},\pi] the tent \pi-x is lower
Hence the area is 2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}x\sin x dx+2\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}(\pi-x)dx = 2(1)+2(\frac{\pi^{2}}{8})
The total 2+\frac{\pi^{2}}{4} matches option B → (B)
3019:
Since |\sin x| is even and \sin x \geq 0 on [0,2], its share is 2\int_{0}^{2}\sin x dx = 2(1-\cos 2)
Also x\sin x is even, rising from 0 to 2\sin 2 < 2, so [x\sin x] is 1 exactly where x\sin x \geq 1
Let c in (0,2) be the unique root of c\sin c = 1; by symmetry the box share is 2(2-c)
Comparing 2(3-\cos 2)-2c with 2(3-\cos 2)+\beta gives \beta = -2c, so \beta\sin\frac{\beta}{2} = 2c\sin c = 2
This value matches option B → (B)
3020:
Separating gives \frac{dy}{1-y+y^{2}} = (1+x+x^{2})dx, and completing the square yields \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{-1}\frac{2y-1}{\sqrt{3}} = x+\frac{x^{2}}{2}+\frac{x^{3}}{3}+C
The condition y(0) = \frac{1}{2} forces C = 0
At x = 1 the right side is \frac{11}{6}, so 2y(1)-1 = \sqrt{3}\tan\frac{11\sqrt{3}}{12}
This expression matches option C → (C)
3021:
Let a, b, c count heads in tosses 1-3, 4-6 and 7-8, needing a+b = 4 with b+c = 3
With b = 1, 2 or 3 the combo counts are \binom{3}{3}\binom{3}{1}\binom{2}{2}+\binom{3}{2}\binom{3}{2}\binom{2}{1}+\binom{3}{1}\binom{3}{3}\binom{2}{0} = 3+18+3 = 24
Out of 2^{8} = 256 equally likely outcomes p = \frac{24}{256} = \frac{3}{32}
Hence 96p = 9 → (9)
3022:
The parabola latus rectum is x = k with endpoints (k,\pm 2k), while the ellipse one is x = ae with endpoints (ae,\pm\frac{b^{2}}{a})
Coinciding gives k = ae and 2k = \frac{b^{2}}{a}, hence 2ae = a(1-e^{2})
So e^{2}+2e-1 = 0 gives e = \sqrt{2}-1, and e^{2} = 3-2\sqrt{2}
Therefore e^{2}+2\sqrt{2} = 3 → (3)
3025:
The switch 3x^{2}-6x+2 = 0 gives corners at x = 1\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, two points where the max changes branch
The factor |x-1| adds a corner at x = 1, where |\cos(x^{2}-\frac{1}{4})| is nonzero
The cosine factor corners where x^{2} = \frac{1}{4}+\frac{\pi}{2}+k\pi, giving x = \pm 1.349, \pm 2.228, \pm 2.847 inside (-\pi,\pi)
No overlaps occur, so 2+1+6 = 9 non-differentiable points → (9)
3034:
Extension under load follows Hooke law, \Delta L = \frac{FL}{AY} with F = 0.8 \times 10 = 8 N
For string A this gives \Delta L_{A} = 1 mm using L_{A} = 0.314 m, Y_{A} = 2 \times 10^{10} in SI units and r = 0.2 mm
String B has twice length and twice modulus so same extension, total \Delta L_{A} + \Delta L_{B} = 2 mm → (B)
3038:
Each bit pair of A and B passes through the gate combination
Evaluating all four bit positions gives output bits 1, 1, 0, 1 in order
Reading the four-bit word gives Y = 1101 → (A)
3039:
Mirror formula with sign convention is \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} with f = -10 cm
Nearer end u_{1} = -20 cm gives v_{1} = -20 cm and farther end u_{2} = -30 cm gives v_{2} = -15 cm
Image length is |v_{1} - v_{2}| = |-20 + 15| = 5 cm → (B)
3041:
Spiral winding gives moment M = N I \pi times mean square radius, M = \frac{1}{3}N I \pi(r_{1}^{2} + r_{1}r_{2} + r_{2}^{2})
Substituting N = 200, I = 20 mA, r_{1} = 3 cm and r_{2} = 6 cm
Evaluation gives M = 2.64 \times 10^{-2} in SI units, so \alpha = 2.64 → (B)
3042:
Forward-biased diode offers 10 ohm in series with 100 ohm resistor
Equivalent charging resistance is R_{eq} = 100 + 10 = 110 in SI units
Time constant is \tau = R_{eq}C = 110 \times 20 \times 10^{-6} = 2.2 \times 10^{-3} s, so \alpha = 2.2 → (A)
3043:
Applying Kirchhoff laws at the junction between A and B fixes the branch currents
Open-circuit potential difference evaluates to 24 V across A and B
Equivalent resistance draws total current 4 A between A and B → (B)
3045:
At Brewster angle reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular and reflected light is fully polarized
Only vibration perpendicular to plane of incidence survives in reflection
That transverse sinusoidal field matches the stated field form → (A)
3047:
Soap film has two surfaces so work is W = 2T\Delta A with \Delta A = 4\pi(r_{2}^{2} - r_{1}^{2})
Substituting T = 3.5 \times 10^{-2}, r_{1} = 1 cm and r_{2} = 2 cm
Evaluation with \pi = \frac{22}{7} gives W = 264 \times 10^{-6} J, so \alpha = 264 → (264)
3048:
SHM velocity satisfies v^{2} = \omega^{2}(A^{2} - x^{2}) so comparison with v^{2} = 50 - x^{2} gives \omega^{2} = 1
Angular frequency is therefore \omega = 1 in SI units
Period is T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi = \frac{44}{7} s, so x = 44 → (44)
3050:
Power factor is \cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z} = 0.5 with R = 100 in SI units
Impedance is therefore Z = 200 in SI units
Reactive part is |X_{L} - X_{C}| = \sqrt{Z^{2} - R^{2}} = 100\sqrt{3}, so \alpha = 100 → (100)
3051:
At STP one mole of gas occupies 22.4 \text{L}, so moles of SO_{2} equal volume divided by molar volume.
Express amount as n = \frac{1.4187}{22.4} \text{mol} = 0.0633 \text{mol} and multiply by Avogadro number.
Count molecules as 0.0633 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.812 \times 10^{22} matching option B → (B)
3052:
Recall wavenumber equals R_{H} \times (\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}) for hydrogen lines.
First Balmer line uses n_{1} = 2 and n_{2} = 3 giving v_{B} = R_{H} \times \frac{5}{36}.
First Brackett line uses n_{1} = 4 and n_{2} = 5 giving v_{Br} = R_{H} \times \frac{9}{400}, so ratio written as 5 : 0.81 matches option B → (B)
3053:

A 4s electron has principal number n = 4 and azimuthal number l = 0 with m = 0.
Single 4s electron takes spin s = +\frac{1}{2}, matching option D → (D)
3054:
For an ideal gas C_{p} - C_{v} = R, so heat capacity at constant pressure exceeds that at constant volume and Statement I is false.
At constant volume no boundary work is done and heat goes to internal energy, so Statement II is true.
False plus true corresponds to option D → (D)
3055:
Dividing a balanced equation by 3 raises its equilibrium constant to power \frac{1}{3}.
Compute K_{2} = K^{\frac{1}{3}} = (2.7 \times 10^{-5})^{\frac{1}{3}} = (27 \times 10^{-6})^{\frac{1}{3}}.

3056:
Count electrons lost with Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} giving one electron and C_{2}O_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 2CO_{2} giving two electrons.
Totals are 3 from FeC_{2}O_{4}, 6 from Fe_{2}(C_{2}O_{4})_{3}, 1 from FeSO_{4} and 0 from Fe_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}, summing to 10 electrons.

3057:
First order decay obeys [R] = [R_{0}]e^{-k_{1}t} where k_{1} is the rate constant.
Fraction remaining is \frac{[R]}{[R_{0}]} = e^{-k_{1}t}, so fraction decomposed is one minus this quantity.
Result 1 - e^{-k_{1}t} matches option D → (D)
3058:
Anion A^{-} with 36 electrons comes from an atom with 35 electrons, so atomic number Z = 35 which is bromine.
Mass number equals protons plus neutrons, giving 35 + 45 = 80.
Bromine lies in group 17 and is liquid at room temperature, matching option A → (A)
3059:
Oxygen normally shows covalency 2 but can expand to 4 using lone pairs, and oxidation states of -2 in SO_{2} and +2 in OF_{2} are correct.
Small size and high electronegativity make oxygen anomalous among group 16 elements.
Both statements are true, matching option A → (A)
3060:
Higher oxidation states grow more stable down a group, so Mo(VI) and W(VI) exceed Cr(VI) and statement A is false.
Ce^{4+} and Tb^{4+} gain stability by reduction while Eu^{2+} and Yb^{2+} gain stability by oxidation, so statement B is true.
Actinoid contraction exceeds lanthanoid contraction while the Cm claim fails, so only B and D hold matching option C → (C)
3061:
Dichromate oxidises Fe^{2+} to Fe^{3+} in acid and chromate and dichromate interconvert with pH, so A and C are true.
Sodium dichromate is hygroscopic and cannot serve as primary standard while potassium dichromate can, so B is false.
Cr-O-Cr angle of 126^{\circ} in Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-} is correct, so A plus C plus D matches option B → (B)
3062:
Weak field water gives high spin counts of 4 for Cr^{2+}, 3 for Co^{2+}, 1 for Cu^{2+} and 5 for Mn^{2+}.
Spin only values \mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} give 4.90 and 3.87 and 1.73 and 5.92 \text{BM} respectively.
Order A-III plus B-I plus C-IV plus D-II matches option D → (D)
3063:
Compare combined inductive and resonance withdrawal with -NO_{2} strongest and -I weakest among the set.
Carboxyl -COOH withdraws less than cyano -CN because cyano has stronger triple bond withdrawal.
Increasing order d then b then a then c matches option C → (C)
3064:
Treat each carbonyl product as a cleaved C=C unit and rejoin carbonyl carbons to rebuild the alkene skeleton.
Two terminal =CH_{2} units account for two formaldehyde molecules while the keto aldehyde and diketone fragments fix the remaining substituted double bonds.
Only the dimethyl dimethylene cyclohexene isomer labelled structure 3 reconstructs all four fragments together.

3065:
Finkelstein exchanges alkyl halide with NaI while Swarts forms alkyl fluorides with SbF_{3}.
Sandmeyer replaces diazonium by chloro using Cu_{2}Cl_{2} while Fittig couples aryl halides with Na in dry ether.
Pairing A-III plus B-I plus C-IV plus D-II matches option B → (B)
3066:
Aqueous NaOH dissolves phenols and carboxylic acids but not aldehydes and alcohols and hydrocarbons and amines.
Phenols II plus III plus IV and acids V plus VII dissolve while benzaldehyde and amino hydrocarbon and hindered hydrocarbon and primary alcohol do not.
Count of soluble compounds equals 5 matching option A → (A)
3067:
Bromination of aniline in water gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline as major product A by ortho and para substitution.
Diazotisation with NaNO_{2} and HCl at 273-278 \text{K} converts A to the corresponding diazonium salt B.
Replacement of diazo group by nitro with NaNO_{2} and Cu on heating gives 1,3,5-tribromo-2-nitrobenzene as C matching option B → (B)
3068:
A disaccharide with a free hemiacetal anomeric carbon acts as a reducing sugar.
Both maltose and lactose retain one free anomeric end in the shown structures, so both are reducing.
Statement I calling maltose nonreducing is false while Statement II calling lactose reducing is true matching option D → (D)
3069:
One letter codes are R for arginine and D for aspartic acid and K for lysine and E for glutamic acid.
Lysine and arginine are essential while aspartic acid and glutamic acid are nonessential in this classification.
Pairing A-II plus B-I plus C-IV plus D-III matches option A → (A)
3070:
Phenolphthalein forms a pink quinoid dianion in dilute NaOH by lactone ring opening.
Excess concentrated alkali adds hydroxide to the central carbon giving a carbinol trianion that breaks conjugation.
Loss of conjugation makes X colourless matching option D → (D)
3071:
Xenon in XeO_{6}^{4-} uses all eight valence electrons in six Xe-O sigma bonds with expanded octet.
Octahedral geometry leaves zero lone pairs on the central xenon atom.
Sum of sigma pairs plus lone pairs equals 6 + 0 = 6 → (6)
3072:
Friedel Crafts methylation followed by chlorination gives predominantly para chlorotoluene from benzene.
Strong oxidation converts the benzylic methyl to carboxyl giving para chlorobenzoic acid X with M = 156.5 \text{g mol}^{-1}.
Each acid liberates one CO_{2} with NaHCO_{3}, so 11.2 \text{L} at STP equals 0.5 \text{mol} and mass equals 0.5 \times 156.5 \text{g} = 78.25 \text{g} → (78.25)
3073:
Carius bromine appears as AgBr precipitate, so moles of bromine equal mass of precipitate divided by molar mass of AgBr.
From 3.36 \text{g} precipitate bromine mass gives about 71.5 percent bromine while carbon is given as 26.7 percent and remainder is hydrogen.
Mole ratio C to Br to H reduces to 2.5 : 1 : 2, doubling gives C_{5}H_{4}Br_{2} type empirical unit with 5 carbons → (5)
3074:
Mixture of NH_{4}OH and NH_{4}Cl forms a basic buffer with pOH = pK_{b} + \log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}.
Ratio equals \frac{250}{5} = 50, so pOH = 4.74 + \log 50 = 4.74 + 1.70 = 6.44.
Result pH = 14 - 6.44 = 7.56 = 756 \times 10^{-2}, so \alpha = 756 → (756)
3075:
At 320 \text{K} apply Raoult law with relative lowering equal to solute mole fraction.
Compute \frac{760 - 750}{760} = \frac{1}{76}, so solvent mole fraction equals \frac{75}{76}.
For the stated composition this mole fraction corresponds to 5 moles of solvent → (5)
